follow_up.reference: The test is two-sided and the normal distribution is symmetric. Equally extreme outcomes in the opposite tail also count.

instances.text: Your test has absolute z 2.68. The standard normal table gives upper tail 0.37 percent. Treat that entry as exact. Across 2 comparisons, what is the Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided p-value, capped at one?
instances.spoken_text: Your test has absolute z two point six eight. The standard normal table gives upper tail zero point three seven percent. Treat that entry as exact. Across two comparisons, what is the Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided p-value, capped at one?

follow_up.question: Does Bonferroni require the tests to be independent?
follow_up.reference: No, its familywise error bound follows from a union bound. Dependence can make it conservative but does not invalidate that bound.
